metadata.title: Socioeconomic Status in PIRLS 2021: Insights from Parent, Student, and Principal Reports
metadata.venue: Boston College, TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report uses PIRLS 2021 Home, Student, and School Questionnaire data and applies sampling weights at both the student and school levels to ensure the multilevel estimates represent the target populations. The HLM models are fit separately by country and include random intercepts for schools, with fixed effects for level-1 slopes; weights are applied to account for the complex survey design and the nested sampling of students within schools. The manuscript does not name a specific weight variable (e.g., W_FSTUWT/TOTWGT), but it explicitly states that sampling weights were applied at both levels. Because the analysis is not ML-based prediction, replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife) are not described; uncertainty is handled within the HLM framework using the weighted estimation approach.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This report does not model cognitive achievement using PIRLS plausible values as the dependent variable; instead, it analyzes the Home Socioeconomic Status scale and its alignment with other questionnaire-based SES indicators, plus HLM variance decomposition of home SES. Plausible values are therefore not applicable to the primary outcome(s) in this report. Missing data handling is described in terms of exclusions for missing SES-scale components and missing predictor variables in specific HLM models, but the report does not provide a single, general missing-data imputation strategy for all variables, so a dedicated missing-data handling label is not fully specified.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report includes all students with available Home SES data and their schools from PIRLS 2021 participating countries. For HLM Models 0–3, observations are excluded if they have missing data on the student-reported number of books at home or the principal-reported school composition of student background. For Model 4, additional exclusions are applied: observations are removed if they have missing data on any of the student- or principal-reported SES-related variables listed in Exhibit 2. Slovak Republic is not included in Model 4 due to unavailability of school composition data, and in Israel the variable indicating whether a student has their own room is missing for the entire country, so exclusions are applied only when other student-reported variables or school composition data are missing. For the Home SES scale itself, a score is provided only if at least two of the four Home SES items are answered (omitting at least three items or not responding to the entire Home Questionnaire yields missing Home SES).

data.outcome_summary: This PIRLS 2021 Insights report examines how socioeconomic status (SES) is conceptualized and measured using a new Home Socioeconomic Status scale derived from the Home Questionnaire completed by parents/guardians of fourth-grade students. The Home SES scale classifies students into higher, middle, and lower SES based on four parent-reported indicators (books, children’s books, parental education, and parental occupation), and the report evaluates its alignment with student-reported home resources (e.g., number of books, access to digital devices) and principal-reported school socioeconomic composition. Correlation analyses use sampling weights and show that the student-reported number of books has the strongest alignment with parent-reported Home SES (international average Pearson r = 0.46; η² = 0.23), while digital-device indicators show much weaker or near-zero associations. The report also uses hierarchical linear modeling (HLM) with random intercepts for schools to quantify how much variance in parent-reported Home SES can be explained by student- and principal-reported variables, finding substantial between-school variation in many countries (ICC up to 0.60) and an international-average total R² of 0.34 for the full Model 4. A key limitation is selection bias risk: Home SES response rates are lower for lower-achieving students in some countries, which can affect interpretation of alignment and explained-variance results.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an IEA PIRLS Insights report focused on measurement, alignment, and multilevel variance decomposition rather than on training/evaluating machine-learning predictive models. As a result, there are no ML algorithms to extract, no ML target-variable prediction results, and no structured ML main findings. The report does include statistical modeling (HLM) and weighted correlation analyses, but these are not ML techniques under the extraction schema.
